page.text:
Abstract algebra studies sets equipped with operations, asking what can
be proved from the properties of the operations alone, regardless of what
the elements are. This chapter climbs a ladder of such structures. Each
rung adds one requirement to the one below it: a bare set with an
operation becomes, in turn, a magma, a semigroup, a monoid, and finally a
group, the central object of elementary algebra.
